ai.description: *Ophisops jerdonii* is a small lacertid reaching 45 mm snout-vent length. It features a brownish body with two pale dorsolateral stripes and fused eyelids forming a transparent spectacle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops jerdonii* is best distinguished by its fused lower eyelid, which forms a transparent window over the eye, and the presence of only four supraocular scales.
ai.habitat: *Ophisops jerdonii* inhabits dry, open scrublands and rocky, arid plains across the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate altitudes in sparse vegetation.
ai.behavior: *Ophisops jerdonii* is a diurnal, active forager that frequently darts between low vegetation and rocky outcrops to hunt small insects under the heat of the sun.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops jerdonii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, primarily between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophisops jerdonii* occurs across arid and semi-arid regions of the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the plains of Punjab and Rajasthan to the Deccan Plateau.
